content: CRIM1, or Cysteine-rich motor neuron 1 protein, is a protein encoded by the CRIM1 gene in humans. Function Motor neurons are among the earliest neurons to emerge following the initiation of cell patterning and the onset of cellular differentiation. This differentiation occurs in a ventral-to-dorsal gradient and is at least partially regulated by the concentration of ventrally expressed Sonic Hedgehog protein (SHH; MIM 600725). Members of the TGF-beta family (e.g., TGF-beta1; MIM 190180) can suppress the induction of these neurons. CRIM1 is thought to interact with growth factors that are involved in the differentiation and survival of motor neurons. Clinical Significance Loss of CRIM1 function, as observed in Crim1 KST264 hypomorph mice, leads to the development of chronic kidney disease. This condition is associated with pathological changes such as papillary hypoplasia, functional urinary tract obstruction, ectopic collagen deposition within the endothelium, and tubulointerstitial fibrosis. These pathological features are partially attributed to endothelial epithelial–mesenchymal transition (EMT).
